## Problem Required checks include conditionally-skipped jobs (`visual`, `prisma`, `migration`, `schema-check`, `docker`, and the core `lint`/`test`/`build` etc. when `code == false`). When these jobs are skipped due to path filters, GitHub branch protection shows them as **Expected** forever — blocking merges on PRs where those paths didn't change. ## Fix Add a `ci-status` umbrella job that: - Always runs (`if: always()`) - Depends on all CI jobs - Passes if all deps passed or were skipped - Fails if any dep failed or was cancelled Then update required checks to use only `CI` (the umbrella) instead of individual job names. ## After merge Update branch protection required checks — remove individual job names, add `CI`. Closes INF-853

author: tuo-lei
body:
## Summary

Prometheus-style redesign of cloud insights storage. Instead of storing 1 row per session (N=185+), store 1 row per (user, machine, date) with aggregate counters.

**Before:** 185 sessions → 185 rows, N+1 or batch of 185 writes per sync
**After:** 185 sessions across 31 days → 31 rows, batch of 31 writes per sync

### Schema change
- DROP `session_insights` (old per-session table)
- CREATE `daily_insights` with `UNIQUE(user_id, machine_id, date)`
- Counters: sessions, prompts, tool_calls, edits, duration_ms, cost
- JSON breakdowns: projects, models, providers (for charts, not SQL filtering)

### CLI changes
- `aggregateDailyInsights()` groups local store by date before sending
- Auto-sync runs at most once per calendar day (was every scan)
- Shared `syncInsightsToCloud()` helper (deduplicated)

### Cloud API changes
- `POST /api/insights/sync` accepts `{machineId, machineName, days[]}` 
- `GET /api/insights/summary` merges daily rows across all machines
- Removed `GET /api/insights` (per-session list no longer exists)

### Cost impact
- D1 writes drop from ~185/sync to ~31/sync (6x reduction)
- A user with 1 year of history: 365 rows instead of ~2000
- Malicious user can only write 1 row per machine per day

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] 607 unit tests + 52 E2E tests pass
- [x] Migration tested locally (DROP + CREATE)
- [ ] Deploy worker + run migration remote
- [ ] Verify sync from dashboard to cloud

body:
## Summary

Add minimal oracle test cases for parser failures discovered through hackage package testing.

## Test Cases Added

### 1. Inline Kind Signatures on GADT-style Declarations
- **File**: `StandaloneKindSignatures/standalone-kind-newtype-unlifted.hs`
- **Source**: Fails in `unlifted` package (e.g., `Data/Either/Void.hs`)
- **Issue**: Parser doesn't support inline kind signatures on `newtype`/`data` declarations with GADT syntax
- **Status**: `xfail`

### 2. Operator Patterns
- **File**: `PatternSyntax/operator-pattern.hs`
- **Source**: Fails in `dice` package (e.g., `Data/Random/Dice.hs`)
- **Issue**: Parser doesn't support using operators (like `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`) as pattern variables in function definitions
- **Status**: `xfail`

## Skipped Cases

### xls Package
The `xls` package failure is not a parser gap - it's a CPP preprocessing issue. The package uses custom CPP macros (`CCALL`) that need expansion before parsing. The raw file with unexpanded macros is correctly rejected by both GHC and aihc-parser.

## Test Results

All 1178 oracle tests pass, including the 2 new xfail cases.

author: likebreath
body:
### Background

Since Linux kernel v6.6, the VFIO subsystem has been extended to support a new device access model - VFIO cdev . Together with the "new" IOMMUFD subsystem, advanced features from modern hardware can be fully exposed and utilized in the guest, achieving fully accelerated iommu in the guest.

More details: https://github.com/rust-vmm/vfio/issues/92

Fixes: https://github.com/cloud-hypervisor/cloud-hypervisor/issues/6892

### Summary

- Add `--platform iommufd=on|off` to use vfio cdev with iommufd instead of the legacy vfio container/group interface (default: `off`)
- Add `--platform vfio_p2p_dma=on|off` to control MMIO BAR DMA mapping into the host IOMMU address space (default: `on`); set to `off` on stock kernels with `iommufd=on` to avoid `-EFAULT` from `IOMMU_IOAS_MAP` on `VM_PFNMAP` pages
- Add seccomp rules for iommufd and vfio cdev ioctls
- Add parameterized iommufd integration tests

### Tests

- [x] VFIO runner (Ubuntu 24.04.3 stock kernel v6.8): existing legacy tests and new `test_iommufd_*` tests pass with `iommufd=on,vfio_p2p_dma=off`
- [x] GH200 system (NVIDIA kernel with [PFNMAP workaround](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NV-Kernels/commit/d5c249583491a530fbedb3ff00621067d5d3ff66)): NVMe and GPU passthrough with `iommufd=on,vfio_p2p_dma=on`

author: castrojo
body:
## Summary

Fixes two critical data correctness bugs and one performance issue in the Go stats pipeline (from SO-5 bootc-ecosystem tech assessment).

### SO-35: Stale cache key (Critical G1)

`build-container.yml` was using cache key `tap-history-v1` while `daily-build.yml` uses `tap-history-v4`. This meant the GHCR OCI image build always got a cold/stale cache — the container image had no homebrew trend history at all.

**Fix:** Update both `key` and `restore-keys` from `tap-history-v1-` to `tap-history-v4-`.

### SO-36: Missing data sync steps (Critical G2)

`build-container.yml` only synced homebrew data. The GHCR OCI image was missing testhub, countme, releases, supply-chain, scorecard, and brewfile analytics — a degraded subset of what the Pages site shows.

**Fix:** Add sync steps for:
- `fetch-brewfile-taps`
- `fetch-testhub` (with `testhub-history-v1` cache restore + save)
- `fetch-countme`
- `fetch-releases`
- `fetch-supply-chain`
- `fetch-scorecard`

All steps use `continue-on-error: true` consistent with `daily-build.yml` pattern, so partial API failures don't block the container push. Cache save steps added so trend history accumulates over time.

### SO-38: Fix computeArchStatus O(N×S log S) sort-per-call pattern (Medium/P1)

`computeArchStatus` and `computeLastStatus` were both sorting `store.Snapshots` on every call — an O(N×S log S) pattern that degrades with scale.

**Root cause:** Both functions internally sorted the snapshot slice before iterating, meaning S×N sorts (once per app per function call) instead of one.

**Fix:** Pre-sort `store.Snapshots` newest-first once before the two app-loops in `runFetchTesthub()`. Both `computeArchStatus` and `computeLastStatus` now receive a pre-sorted slice and iterate directly. The contract is documented in each function's godoc.

**Regression tests added** (`cmd/stats/main_test.go`):
- `TestComputeArchStatus_BothKnown` — both arches resolved from newest snapshot
- `TestComputeArchStatus_NewestWins` — newest data takes precedence over older failures
- `TestComputeArchStatus_Failing` — failing result propagated correctly
- `TestComputeArchStatus_UnknownApp` — missing app returns unknown/unknown
- `TestComputeArchStatus_EmptySnapshots` — nil input returns unknown/unknown
- `TestComputeArchStatus_DoesNotMutateInput` — input slice order is not modified by the function
- `TestComputeArchStatus_ArmOnlyResolvesFromOlderSnapshot` — arch independence: each arch resolved independently from its most-recent snapshot

## Testing

- `go test ./...` passes: all 16 packages pass
- actionlint passes on the updated workflow
- Pattern matches `daily-build.yml` structure exactly

author: ulixert
body:
## Summary

When a quorum write hits a dead replica, the coordinator now buffers the write as a hint for later replay. When the target node recovers (transitions to Alive), the drainer replays hints via `ReplicateWriteBatch` and deletes them from the store. This is the fast-path repair mechanism; anti-entropy (PR 8) is the safety net for longer outages.

## Key design decisions

- **Separate `db.DB` for hints** with `DisableWALSync: true` — hints are ephemeral (24h TTL, 256MB cap), so crash-loss is acceptable and skipping fsync dramatically reduces write latency.
- **Reserve-then-write capacity accounting** — `writeMu` only protects fast arithmetic (cap check + size increment); `db.Put` happens outside the lock so WAL I/O never blocks other hint writers.
- **Delete-then-decrement on Remove** — prevents accounting drift; size is only decremented after successful `db.Delete`.
- **Batch replay via `ReplicateWriteBatch`** — dual-bounded by `MaxBatchBytes` (512KB) and `MaxBatchItems` (500), whichever limit hits first. Adapts naturally to both tiny KV values and large vector payloads (~3KB).
- **Membership-gated sweep** — periodic sweep only triggers drains for Alive targets, avoiding wasted RPCs to Dead nodes.
- **Original envelope preserved exactly** — hint value is the raw `EncodeEnvelope` output, replayed as-is. No timestamp reconstruction. Duplicates are harmless due to LWW with HLC timestamps.
- **Two-phase iteration** — expired/corrupt hints are collected during scan, then deleted after iterator is closed. This avoids a deadlock between the DB read lock (held by iterator) and write lock (needed by Delete).

## Files changed

| File | Type | LOC | Description |
|------|------|-----|-------------|
| `wal/wal.go` | Modified | +18 | `noSync` field, conditional `Sync()` in `WriteEntries` |
| `wal/wal_test.go` | Modified | +33 | Updated `Create` calls, `TestWAL_NoSync` |
| `db/db.go` | Modified | +3 | `DisableWALSync` option, plumbed to WAL |
| `db/read.go` | Modified | +21 | `ScanPrefix`, `prefixSuccessor` |
| `db/db_test.go` | Modified | +51 | `TestDB_ScanPrefix`, `TestDB_ScanPrefix_AllFF` |
| `cluster/hintedhandoff/store.go` | **New** | 285 | Hint store with reserve-then-write capacity |
| `cluster/hintedhandoff/store_test.go` | **New** | 295 | 8 tests: round-trip, isolation, cap, concurrency, etc. |
| `cluster/hintedhandoff/drain.go` | **New** | 382 | Drainer with batch replay + membership-gated sweep |
| `cluster/hintedhandoff/drain_test.go` | **New** | 459 | 6 tests: replay, retry, TTL, dedup, dead-skip, batching |
| `cluster/coordinator.go` | Modified | +16 | `hintStore` field, `SetHintStore`, dead-node branch |

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race -count=3 ./wal/...` — WAL noSync behavior
- [x] `go test -race -count=3 ./db/...` — ScanPrefix + DisableWALSync plumbing
- [x] `go test -race -count=3 ./cluster/hintedhandoff/...` — store + drainer
- [x] `go test -race ./...` — no regressions (all 18 packages pass)

body: ## Summary Adds `Cache-Control` header preservation to the S3 service, following the exact same pattern as the existing `Content-Encoding` support. Previously, `Cache-Control` set on `PutObject` was silently dropped — `GetObject` and `HeadObject` would not return it. This broke consumers (e.g. seadn's `fallback-processing` test) that rely on `CacheControl` metadata surviving a put/get round-trip. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (`fix:`) - [x] New feature (`feat:`) - [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`) - [ ] Docs / chore ## AWS Compatibility Real AWS S3 stores and returns the `Cache-Control` header as a first-class object property (not user metadata). This change mirrors that behavior. The `CopyObject` REPLACE directive logic matches AWS: when `x-amz-metadata-directive: REPLACE` is set, the new `Cache-Control` value is used; otherwise the source object's value is preserved. ## Key review areas - **Overload chain** (`S3Service.java`): `cacheControl` is threaded through `putObject` (4 overloads) and `storeObject` (3 overloads) via positional params. Verify the null-arg counts are correct in each delegation call — a wrong count would silently misalign parameters. - **CopyObject REPLACE logic** (`S3Service.copyObject`): `effectiveCacheControl` follows the same conditional as `effectiveContentEncoding` — only replaced when directive is `REPLACE` *and* a new value is provided. - **Not included**: Multipart upload path does not set `cacheControl`, consistent with how `contentEncoding` is handled today. ## Checklist - [x] `./mvnw test` passes locally (1609 tests, 0 failures) - [x] New or updated integration test added (6 tests: put, get, head, copy-preserve, copy-replace, cleanup) - [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/06b7e28f3e664783b17ed18060e5c267 Requested by: @Meemaw ---

author: futuroptimist
body:
### Motivation
- The `/docs` landing currently hydrates a large per-doc payload (full stripped body text + features) and does client-side full-text/snippet work on every keystroke, increasing payload, hydration, and CPU cost.
- The goal is a narrow, low-risk v3.0.1 design that reduces initial payload and perceived typing latency while preserving existing search semantics (`has:` operators, snippet parity) and offline/SSR safety.
- This change is design-only: it proposes an implementation-ready plan without altering runtime behavior or application code.

### Description
- Added `docs/design/docs-index-performance-and-presentation.md`, which documents the problem statement, current-state analysis with concrete code anchors (`frontend/src/pages/docs/index.astro`, `DocsIndex.svelte`, `frontend/src/lib/docs/fullTextSearch.ts`, `frontend/src/utils/docsSearchFeatures.js`, `frontend/src/utils/docsSkillsIndex.js`, `frontend/src/pages/docs/json/sections.json`), measured facts (payload estimates ~356 KB enriched vs ~5.5 KB baseline), hypotheses, risks, and UX rough edges.
- Compared multiple candidate approaches (micro-optimizations, payload split + lazy index, build-time compressed index, precomputed snippets) and recommended a conservative two-tier payload approach: ship a light browse manifest and defer full-text corpus load on first non-empty query, plus query-time caching and small presentation polish.
- Included concrete, minimal implementation slices (2–4 PR-sized changes), rollout and verification plan, acceptance criteria for v3.0.1, and explicit deferrals for v3.1+ (ranking, inverted-index redesign, analytics, worker offload).
- Kept repo workflow guidance centralized (no AGENTS.md changes), preserved SSR/offline constraints, and emphasized test/QA gates tied to existing test suites and `node scripts/link-check.mjs`.

body:
The official `mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512` model stores linear weights as `float8_e4m3fn` with per-tensor `weight_scale_inv` scale factors. Without handling this, the builder either misroutes loading through `QuantModel` (due to `quantization_config` in the config) or feeds raw FP8 tensors into the ONNX graph, both of which fail.

## Changes

- **`modelbuilder/builders/mistral.py`**: Add `_dequantize_fp8_weights(model)` that walks all modules and, for any with a `float8_e4m3fn` weight and a `weight_scale_inv` buffer, dequantizes in-place:
  ```python
  weight_fp32 = weight_fp8.float() * weight_scale_inv
  ```
  `Ministral3TextModel.load_weights()` now calls this after loading for both the `ForCausalLM` and `ConditionalGeneration` paths.

- **`modelbuilder/builder.py`**: Strip `quantization_config` from the HF config before constructing the model object for both `Ministral3ForCausalLM` and `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`. This prevents the base class from routing through `QuantModel.from_pretrained()`, which has no FP8 support.

- **`tests/fast/test_random_ministral3.py`**: Two unit tests for `_dequantize_fp8_weights`: no-op on float32 weights, and correct scale application on `float8_e4m3fn` weights.

body: ## Summary Implements Git-compatible shallow submodule behavior for `clone --recurse-submodules` and `submodule update`, matching `t5614-clone-submodules-shallow`. ## Changes - Parse `submodule..shallow` from `.gitmodules` (true/false). - Add `--no-shallow-submodules` on `clone`. - Add `submodule update --no-recommend-shallow`. - Apply `--depth 1` to submodule clones when: - `--shallow-submodules` is set, or - `.gitmodules` recommends shallow (and not overridden by `--no-recommend-shallow` / `--no-shallow-submodules`). - A shallow **superproject** alone does **not** imply shallow submodules (per t5614). - Propagate `clone` shallow flags to the follow-up `submodule update` via `GRIT_CLONE_SHALLOW_SUBMODULES` / `GRIT_CLONE_NO_SHALLOW_SUBMODULES` so `separate-git-dir` submodule clones get the same rules. - Fix `clone` when `--directory` is omitted: clone `args.directory` instead of moving it so `clone_submodules` can still read clone flags. ## Validation - `./scripts/run-tests.sh t5614-clone-submodules-shallow.sh` (9/9) - `cargo test -p grit-lib --lib`

author: smolkaj
body:
## Summary

\`prepare_test_module_repo\` runs \`bazel vendor\` with
\`USE_BAZEL_VERSION=latest\`, which resolves the module graph under a
Bazel version that may differ from what the module actually targets.
This causes spurious failures when a transitive dep is compatible with
the module's declared Bazel version but not with \`latest\`.

**Example:** \`grpc@1.80.0\` declares \`rules_swift@2.5.0\` (compat
level 2). Bazel 9's \`bazel_tools\` bundles \`rules_swift@3.1.2\`
(compat level 3). The vendor step fails even though the module only
targets Bazel 7/8 and works fine there.

## Fix

Read the module's \`presubmit.yml\` before vendoring and use the
highest Bazel version from the matrix (across both top-level tasks
and \`bcr_test_module\`). Falls back to \`"latest"\` if no version is
configured.

Tested locally against three modules:
- \`grpc@1.80.0\`: {7.x, 8.x} → 8.x
- \`fourward@20260405.1\`: {8.x} → 8.x
- \`p4c@1.2.5.11.bcr.1\`: {7.x, 8.x, 9.x} → 9.x

Fixes bazelbuild/bazel-central-registry#8331. cc @fmeum

author: fazxes
body:
## Problem

Eval #0017 showed `counters.fixes = 3` despite only 1 real fix commit. The agent used a count-only payload (`fixes_committed: 1`) and the parser stored `fixes_count_only = 1` on the `CycleResult`. However, `append_cycle_state()` in `core/state.py` never checked `fixes_count_only` -- it fell through to the commit-count fallback, which counted all commits (fix + shift-log), inflating the counter.

Additionally, `cycles[0].fixes = []` in state.json because no structured fix objects exist when the agent uses count-only payloads (this is expected -- we cannot synthesize fix objects from a count).

## Root Cause

`append_cycle_state()` checked `fixes_count_only` only indirectly through the verifier functions (`expected_fix_commits`, `allowed_total_cycle_commits`) but never used it to compute `inferred_fix_count` for the state counter update.

The fallback path:
```python
if not fixes and not logged_issues and verification["commits"] and not state["log_only_mode"]:
    inferred_fix_count = len(verification["commits"])  # wrong: counted ALL commits
```
...fired when it should not have (when `fixes_count_only` was already set).

## Fix

`nightshift/core/state.py` -- `append_cycle_state()`: when `fixes` list is empty, check `cycle_result.fixes_count_only` first. Only fall back to commit count when that field is absent or zero.

## Tests

Three new regression tests added to `TestAppendCycleState`:
- `test_count_only_payload_uses_fixes_count_not_commit_count` -- primary regression: 1 fix, 2 commits -> counter = 1
- `test_count_only_payload_does_not_trigger_empty_cycle` -- count-only cycle with commits must not increment empty_cycles
- `test_count_only_payload_with_zero_count_falls_back_to_commits` -- `fixes_count_only=0` (falsy) still uses commit fallback

## Verification

`make check` passes: 1159 tests, ruff, mypy, dry-runs all green.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `ape-shell` — a drop-in shell replacement that routes every command through `apes run --shell` for grant-based authorization
- New `--shell` flag on `apes run` with session grant reuse (`runShellMode`)
- argv[0] detection in `cli.ts`: when invoked as `ape-shell`, rewrites args to `apes run --shell -- bash -c <cmd>`
- New `bin.ape-shell` entry in package.json
- README and CLI docs page covering installation, usage, and AI agent sandboxing

## How it works

\`\`\`
AI Agent: \$SHELL -c \"git status\"
  ↓  SHELL=/usr/local/bin/ape-shell
ape-shell -c \"git status\"
  ↓  argv[0] detection → rewrite
apes run --shell -- bash -c \"git status\"
  ↓  runShellMode
1. Find existing ape-shell session grant (timed/always) → execute
2. No grant → request + wait for approval → execute
\`\`\`

First command triggers a session grant request. Human approves once (e.g. \`grant_type: timed, duration: 8h\`) and all subsequent commands reuse the same grant without interaction. Revoke the grant to immediately stop the agent.

## Use case

Sandboxing AI coding agents (OpenClaw, Claude Code, etc.) so they can only execute commands the human has pre-approved. Works transparently — no changes to the agent code, just set \`SHELL=ape-shell\`.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm turbo run test --filter=@openape/apes\` — 253 tests pass (8 new)
- [x] \`pnpm turbo run typecheck\` — clean
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` — clean
- [x] Manual: \`ape-shell --version\` shows version

## Summary

Replace the separate pull_request.yaml and image-build.yaml with a single ci.yaml that triggers on both pull_request and push to main. On pull_request, only the build, lint, test, and test-e2e jobs run. On push to main, those same jobs run first, and after ci-complete gates them, the per-arch binary builds and image assembly proceed (guarded by `if: github.event_name == 'push'`).

This eliminates the double build on merge to main where both workflows previously ran the full test suite independently. The image build is now gated on all checks passing within the same workflow run. The Go cache is also simpler: the same build job saves on main and restores on PRs, with no cross-workflow cache indirection.

author: tmartin2113
body:
## Summary

Adds two operator-side helpers and a README section for the `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR` override that landed in [paperclipai/paperclip#3178](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/3178) and [tmartin2113/paperclip#17](https://github.com/tmartin2113/paperclip/pull/17) (already in `ghcr.io/tmartin2113/paperclip-server:latest`).

No runtime behavior changes to Vibe-Stack's Python code — this is pure tooling.

## What this adds

### `scripts/check-paperclip-skills.sh`

Doctor-style verification. Runs `docker exec` against `vibe-stack-server-1` and:

1. Confirms the container is running.
2. Reads `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR` from inside the container (warns if unset so you know to rebuild / override).
3. Asserts the directory exists and contains `paperclip/SKILL.md` (the core heartbeat skill).
4. Lists every skill folder with its `SKILL.md` line count and first `# heading` — a quick sanity check without opening any file.
5. Warns if `/paperclip/.npm/_npx/*` still contains a stale `@paperclipai` npx cache from earlier bootstrap paths.

Example output against today's container (before pulling the new image):

```
 OK  container 'vibe-stack-server-1' is running
WARN PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR is not set inside the container
 OK  /app/skills exists and is a directory
 OK  core heartbeat skill present: /app/skills/paperclip/SKILL.md

== skills in /app/skills ==
  paperclip                       416 lines  Paperclip Skill
  paperclip-create-agent          140 lines  Paperclip Create Agent Skill
  create-agent-adapter            719 lines  Creating a Paperclip Agent Adapter
  release                         403 lines  Release Coordination Skill
  release-changelog               364 lines  Release Changelog Skill
  memory                           84 lines  Shared Memory
  para-memory-files               105 lines  PARA Memory Files
  skill-discovery                  70 lines  Skill Discovery

== stale npx skill cache ==
WARN stale @paperclipai npx caches found in /paperclip/.npm/_npx/:
    281M /paperclip/.npm/_npx/43414d9b790239bb
```

### `scripts/cleanup-paperclip-skill-cache.sh`

Purges stale `/paperclip/.npm/_npx/*` caches from the persistent `paperclip-data` volume. On a volume that's been through multiple upgrade paths the cache can be **hundreds of MB** of orphaned `@paperclipai` package metadata from earlier `npx paperclipai` bootstrap steps — the fork-built server image no longer uses that flow, but the caches hang around silently.

- Dry-run by default — shows what would be deleted
- `--apply` to actually delete
- Honors `SERVER_CONTAINER=<name>` if you've renamed the container

### README

New "Paperclip Skill Management" section under Configuration explaining:
- The `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR` contract
- Both scripts and their use cases
- The typical first-time cleanup flow

## Motivation

With `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR` now honored by all five `*-local` adapters upstream + in the fork, operators need a way to:

1. **Verify** which skills their production server is actually serving — not inferred from build metadata.
2. **Reclaim disk** from stale npx caches that sit on the persistent volume across upgrades.
3. **Eventually** (follow-up PR, not here) bind-mount a host directory for runtime skill swapping from Vibe-Stack's Python skill registry.

## What's NOT in this PR (intentional)

- **No `docker-compose.yml` change**. The published image already bakes `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR=/app/skills`, so there's nothing to override yet. Adding a compose env var now would either be a no-op (same value) or would require designing where Vibe-Stack's Python skill system writes to — and that's a bigger design discussion that touches skill security (`agents/skill_security.py`).
- **No Python doctor integration**. `agents/doctor.py` runs in the Vibe-Stack agent context, not the server container, so it can't cheaply check `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR` inside the server. A bash script that `docker exec`s the server is the right tool here.

Both are explicitly deferred for a follow-up that handles the runtime-skill-swapping design end-to-end.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/check-paperclip-skills.sh` runs clean against the current running container (screenshot above)
- [x] `scripts/cleanup-paperclip-skill-cache.sh` dry-run correctly identifies the 281M stale cache
- [ ] After user pulls the new image + restarts, check script shows `PAPERCLIP_SKILLS_DIR=/app/skills` and no warning
- [ ] After `--apply`, check script shows no stale npx cache warning

author: revdan
body:
Three defence-in-depth fixes for invariants whose only enforcement was the absence of an Ash action. The policy hardening sweep closed the application-layer holes; this migration closes the direct-SQL-layer holes that the threat model matrix surfaced as gaps.

## Changes

### 1. `operator_signing_keys` append-only trigger

`BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` rejects all mutations. The table is documented as append-only (rotation creates a new row), but only the absence of an Ash update action enforced it. Direct SQL could silently mutate or remove a row, breaking "old receipts verify forever."

### 2. `operators.slug` immutability trigger

`BEFORE UPDATE` rejects writes that change the `slug` column. The slug is embedded in every signed operator receipt, so changing it would silently break verification for every existing receipt.

### 3. `api_keys.key_hash` CHECK constraint

Constrains `key_hash` to the canonical bcrypt format (`$2[aby]$NN$<53 chars>`). Added with `NOT VALID` so the migration is safe in environments with unusual historical data.

All three use `session_replication_role = 'replica'` as the documented escape hatch for legitimate one-off interventions.

## Tests

11 new tests in `db_immutability_test.exs` covering each trigger/constraint, plus the legitimate bypass path.

Full umbrella suite: **326 tests, 0 failures** (225 wallop_core, 101 wallop_web).

## Also

- Threat model matrix updated: I-8, I-9, I-10 now have ✅ at the trigger/constraint column
- wallop_core 0.11.1 → 0.11.2

author: tensorlink-dev
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes JSON serialization issues when storing data in PostgreSQL JSONB columns by properly handling float infinity and NaN values, which PostgreSQL's JSONB parser rejects.

## Key Changes
- Added `_sanitize_for_json()` function that recursively replaces `inf` and `nan` float values with `None` before JSON serialization
- Added `_jsonb()` helper function that wraps `json.dumps()` with sanitization for consistent JSONB column serialization
- Updated `element_to_params()` to use `_jsonb()` for all JSONB columns (`loss_curve`, `generated_samples`, `objectives`)
- Applied the same sanitization in `update_frontier()` endpoint to handle frontier data before storage

## Implementation Details
- The sanitization is recursive, handling nested dictionaries and lists
- PostgreSQL's JSONB parser rejects JavaScript-style `Infinity` and `NaN` tokens that Python's default `json.dumps()` emits, so these are converted to SQL `null` values
- This ensures valid JSON is sent to PostgreSQL regardless of statement caching or connection pooling settings

author: himanshp1656
body:
## Problem

Two bugs when using `SqlMetadataExtractor` as a base class:

**Bug 1 — "No Workers Running" in Temporal**
`App.__init_subclass__` used `getattr(cls, "_app_registered", False)` which walks the MRO. After fix #2 below sets `_app_registered = True` on `SqlMetadataExtractor`, concrete subclasses (e.g. `CloudSqlApp`) would inherit that `True` value and be silently skipped during registration — resulting in no worker on their queue.

**Bug 2 — Cleanup activities run multiple times**
Without `_app_registered = True`, `SqlMetadataExtractor` auto-registers and its `run()` gets wrapped with `workflow_run_wrapper`. That wrapper has `on_complete()` cleanup in its `finally` block. When a concrete subclass calls `super().run()`, it hits the wrapped version, firing cleanup prematurely. Then the subclass's own wrapper fires cleanup again — causing cleanup activities (`cleanup_files`, `cleanup_storage`) to run in a loop.

## Fix

1. **`SqlMetadataExtractor`**: set `_app_registered: bool = True` in the class body to opt out of auto-registration. It is a base template, not a concrete app.

2. **`App.__init_subclass__`**: use `cls.__dict__.get("_app_registered", False)` instead of `getattr(...)`. This checks only the class's own namespace — subclasses no longer inherit the flag through the MRO and correctly register themselves.

## Test

Verified end-to-end with `CloudSqlApp` (a `SqlMetadataExtractor` subclass):
- `CloudSqlApp` registers on its own Temporal queue
- `SqlMetadataExtractor` does not register
- Cleanup activities run exactly once after workflow completion

## Problem

The warm pool allocator calls `ListReferrers` on claimed instances to verify they are fully detached from their MIG before handing them to an environment. The runner service account is missing the `compute.instances.listReferrers` permission, causing a 403 error:

```
googleapi: Error 403: Required 'compute.instances.listReferrers' permission for
'projects/gcp-runner-test/zones/us-east1-c/instances/ona-wp-...'
```

The runner proceeds anyway (the check is non-fatal), but the readiness verification is effectively skipped.

## Fix

Add `compute.instances.listReferrers` to the runner custom IAM role and update the runner role docs (`docs/iam.md`, `docs/detailed_iam_reference.md`).

body:
Towers and traps had empty `Update` stubs and no shared enemy interface, making gameplay behavior entirely non-functional. This PR wires up the core combat loop for all three tower types and two of three trap types, and lays the polymorphic foundation needed for targeting.

## Enemy layer

- **`Enemy` base class** — added virtual interface (`isDead`, `getHP`, `getHPMax`, `getGoldValue`, `takeDamage`) plus shred effect helpers (`applyShred`, `isShredded`, `tickEffects`, `shredResistance`)
- **All 5 enemy subclasses** — added `override` keywords, integrated `tickEffects(dt)` + self-`Destroy` on death into each `Update`, applied shred tier-reduction in `takeDamage`
- **`Goblin::takeDamage` bug fix** — damage application was commented out; now correctly applies
- **`EnemyQuery.hpp`** (new) — `GetEnemyComponent(Actor*)` and `GetAllLiveEnemies(World*)` helpers used by all towers/traps to iterate live enemies without coupling to specific types

## EnemyMovement

- `ApplySlow(duration, factor)` — scales movement speed while timer active
- `ApplyStun(duration)` — halts movement entirely for duration
- `GetCheckpointIndex()` — exposes path progress for FIRST/LAST aggro targeting
- `Update` respects stun before slow before normal movement

## Towers

All three towers now implement a full fire cycle: stun check → cooldown tick → target selection → effect application → cooldown reset.

- **`TowerSingle`** — single-target damage; selects via `AggroMode` (FIRST/LAST uses checkpoint index, MAX_HP/CURRENT_HP compares health values); added `stun_timer` + `applyStun()`
- **`TowerAOE`** — picks primary target by `AggroMode`, then damages all enemies within `aoe_radius` of that position; `attack_cooldown` added
- **`TowerCC`** — applies `SLOW` via `EnemyMovement::ApplySlow` or `SHRED` via `Enemy::applyShred`; configurable `cc_duration` (serialized); `attack_cooldown` added

```cpp
// Example: TowerSingle fires at the furthest-progressed enemy in range
case AggroMode::FIRST:
    val = actor->HasComponent<EnemyMovement>()
        ? static_cast<float>(actor->GetComponent<EnemyMovement>().GetCheckpointIndex())
        : 0.0f;
    break;
```

## Traps

- **`TrapMine`** — detects first live enemy within `trigger_radius`, deals physical damage, self-destroys (single-use)
- **`TrapWolf`** — detects first live enemy within `trigger_radius`, calls `EnemyMovement::ApplyStun` with a randomized duration, self-destroys (single-use)
- `trigger_radius` added to both and exposed in `Inspect`/`Serialize`

## Not yet completed

- `TrapAuraGold::Update` — header updated with `m_AwardedActors` tracking set; `.cpp` Update body not implemented
- `TowerManager` / `TrapManager` — stubs remain empty; placement UI, prefab loading, and Magicien death-stun dispatch not implemented
- `TowerManager`/`TrapManager` not yet registered in `GameAssembly.cpp`

author: boomerang9
body:
## Summary

Response to a 5-layer security audit of the ORACLE 8-Gates Verification Framework. Two commits: hardening rewrite + 39 regression tests. Total suite: 47 tests, all green.

## Ship-blocking fixes (5)

1. **Fail-closed try/catch** around every \`gate.run()\` — a throwing gate (e.g. \`spec.query=42\` → \`.trim()\` crash) is caught, logged, and recorded as that gate's failure. Previously this was a remotely-triggerable bypass.
2. **Single \`normalizeSpec()\`** at top of \`runGates()\` — coerces query/intent/userId to safe strings once. Kills 8 duplicated \`spec.query || ''\` fallbacks and the \`(42).trim()\` type hole.
3. **Bounded two-level QueryLRU** — caps total users (10k) + queries-per-user (3) + 1h TTL sweep. Previously unbounded Map → OOM on rotating userIds.
4. **Typed \`OracleSpec\` / \`OracleOutput\` contracts** in new \`oracle/types.ts\` — zero \`any\` in index.ts. \`ACPIntent\` imported from \`../acp/types.ts\`.
5. **LUC scrubbed from user-facing errors** — "LUC failed to produce a cost quote" → "Cost quote could not be generated." Per Dual-Layer Access rule.

## Bonus fixes (6)

6. \`GateCheckResult\` as discriminated union — \`passed: false\` requires \`reason\` at type level
7. Effort gate NaN guard — filters non-finite USD before \`Math.min\`, fails closed if none remain
8. Perception gate surrogate-pair aware — \`for..of\` + \`codePointAt\` so emoji = 1 not 2
9. False-positive regexes pruned (dropped: \`INSERT INTO\`, \`UPDATE SET\`, \`onload=\`, \`__proto__\`, \`|| word\`, \`%27\`, \`%22\`, \`;ls\`)
10. Case-insensitive guest check — \`'Guest'\` / \`'GUEST '\` can't bypass
11. \`Oracle._resetForTesting()\` exposed for test isolation

## Test coverage (39 new tests)

| Suite | Tests | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Fail-closed on gate exception | 5 | ✅ |
| Spec normalization | 3 | ✅ |
| QueryLRU behavior | 4 | ✅ |
| IP protection | 3 | ✅ |
| Perception emoji handling | 3 | ✅ |
| Security false-positive regressions | 14 | ✅ |
| Guest case-insensitivity | 4 | ✅ |
| Discriminated union contract | 1 | ✅ |
| Effort NaN guard | 2 | ✅ |
| **Total new** | **39** | **✅** |
| Original oracle.test.ts | 8 | ✅ |
| **Grand total** | **47** | **✅** |

author: appcypher
body:
## Summary
- Add a uv-managed Python benchmark project under `benchmarks/` that compares filesystem performance between Docker containers and Microsandbox sandboxes using a shared OCI image.
- Ship 14 in-guest workloads grouped into rootfs/read-only (`metadata_scan_stdlib`, `read_all_py_stdlib`, `deep_tree_traverse`, `random_read_stdlib`), write path (`small_file_create_1k`, `mid_file_create_100`, `seq_write_fsync_16m`, `shm_write_fsync_16m`), read-back (`seq_read_16m`, `mmap_read_16m`), lifecycle (`file_delete_1k`, `rename_1k`), and mixed/concurrent (`mixed_read_write`, `concurrent_read_4t`).
- Each workload runs in a fresh Docker container and a fresh msb sandbox to avoid state leakage; the guest reports its own `time.perf_counter()` timings so results reflect the I/O stack as seen by the application rather than just host wall clock. Image pulls are timed separately and `--image` can be repeated to benchmark multiple OCI images in one run.
- Results are written as JSON to `build/bench/fs/` and an aligned summary table is printed with median, msb/docker ratio, and stdev. A `--baseline` flag compares the current run against a saved JSON and prints both raw speedup and a normalized speedup that controls for Docker variance between runs.
- Motivation: there was no repeatable way to measure rootfs and tmpfs behavior across Microsandbox revisions, which made it hard to evaluate proposed filesystem changes. This harness gives a reproducible baseline for that work.

## Test Plan
- [x] `just bench-fs` runs end to end and writes a JSON file under `build/bench/fs/`
- [x] The printed summary table is aligned and shows median, msb/docker ratio, and stdev for each workload
- [x] `cd benchmarks && uv run bench_fs.py --workload metadata_scan_stdlib --workload seq_read_16m` runs only the selected workloads
- [x] `cd benchmarks && uv run bench_fs.py --image python:3.12-slim --image python:3.12` runs all workloads against both images and groups results per image in the JSON and the table
- [x] `cd benchmarks && uv run bench_fs.py --skip-pull` reuses already-pulled images without re-timing the pull
- [x] `cd benchmarks && uv run bench_fs.py --output baselines/before.json` followed by `cd benchmarks && uv run bench_fs.py --msb-bin ../build/msb --baseline baselines/before.json` produces a comparison table with raw and normalized speedup
- [x] Workloads that need setup (`deep_tree_traverse`, `random_read_stdlib`, `seq_read_16m`, `mmap_read_16m`, `mixed_read_write`, `concurrent_read_4t`) and `before_each` (`file_delete_1k`, `rename_1k`) all complete without errors
- [x] `uv sync` in `benchmarks/` succeeds with no external dependencies (stdlib only)

author: jfrancoa
body:
## Summary

- Fix a race condition in the GCS backup module's `Initialize()` access-check that causes collection exports (and potentially backups) to fail deterministically on multi-node clusters
- Each `Initialize()` call now writes and deletes its own unique access-check file, keyed by hostname + atomic counter, so concurrent calls from different nodes never interfere

## Problem

`Initialize()` validates GCS write/delete access by creating a temporary `access-check` object and immediately deleting it. The object path was **not node-specific** — all nodes used the same `{backupID}/access-check` path.

During the export commit phase, the coordinator fans out `commitNode()` to all participants concurrently. Each participant calls `Initialize()` with the same export ID, creating a race on the shared access-check object. The coordinator's local participant consistently wins (warm GCS connection from earlier validation + no gRPC hop), deleting the object before remote nodes reach their `Delete` call → **deterministic 404 on every export attempt**.

## Fix

Give each `Initialize()` call a unique access-check object by appending the node's hostname and a per-client atomic counter:

```
Before: {path}/{exportID}/access-check          ← shared, races
After:  {path}/{exportID}/access-check-weaviate-0-1  ← unique per call
        {path}/{exportID}/access-check-weaviate-1-1
        {path}/{exportID}/access-check-weaviate-2-1
```

Falls back to PID if `os.Hostname()` fails.

### What's being changed:

`modules/backup-gcs/client.go`:
- Add `nodeID` (hostname) and `counter` (atomic uint64) fields to `gcsClient`
- `newClient()` captures hostname at creation time (falls back to PID)
- `Initialize()` builds a unique key per call: `access-check-{nodeID}-{seq}`

- [ ] Performance tests have been run or not necessary.

author: 6ogo
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors how callout blocks (takeaway, pitfall, key) are rendered in the markdown renderer and improves content truncation logic to respect paragraph boundaries.

## Key Changes

- **Simplified callout rendering**: Removed the `extractTextContent()` utility function and recursive markdown re-parsing. Callout components now directly render children instead of extracting text and re-parsing it, reducing complexity and potential double-processing.

- **Improved callout formatting**: Updated regex replacements in `processContent()` to add proper spacing around callout divs with newlines, ensuring better markdown parsing and rendering of the content within callouts.

- **Smarter content truncation**: Changed the preview truncation logic in `LanguagePage.jsx` to cut at paragraph boundaries (double newlines) rather than hard-cutting at 2000 characters, resulting in more natural preview text.

- **Replaced inline link with styled component**: Converted the markdown-embedded "View complete guide" link into a proper styled Link component with border separator, improving UX and consistency with the design system.

- **Cleaned up section extraction**: Updated `markdownLoader.js` to strip trailing horizontal rules (`---`) from extracted section content, preventing unwanted visual separators in the output.

## Implementation Details

The callout rendering simplification is particularly important—previously, the code would extract text from React children, pass it back through ReactMarkdown, and re-render. author: celina-create
body:
## What

Add 4 GitHub Actions workflows to automate issue lifecycle management — triage, response tracking, contributor engagement, and contribution pool health.

## Why

As Nexu's open-source community grows, we need automated systems to ensure:
- Every issue gets properly labeled within seconds of creation
- No issue goes without a team response for >24h
- Contributors get clear guidance when claiming and completing issues
- The contribution pool always has ≥10 good-first-issues available

This directly supports the 3-month goal of reaching 100 effective contributors.

## How

### 1. `issue-triage-bot.yml` — Auto-label on issue open/edit
- **Type detection**: `type:bug` / `type:feature` / `type:i18n` / `type:docs` / `type:skill` (from template labels + keyword matching)
- **Area detection**: `area/frontend` / `area/backend` / `area/skill-engine` / `area/docs` / `area/channels` / `area/credit` (rich keyword patterns including Chinese)
- **Platform detection**: `windows` label
- **Priority auto-suggestion**: P0 (crash/data loss) → P1 (broken feature) → P2 (cosmetic)
- **Good First Issue auto-detection**: Identifies UX-visible issues based on user experience signals (e.g. "找不到", "不能拖动", "显示异常", "missing button"). Criteria: UX signal match + single area + no deep architecture + is a bug
- **Welcome message**: First-time contributors get a welcome comment with guidance
- **Process label**: `needs-triage` added when no priority is set

### 2. `issue-response-tracker.yml` — 24h SLA enforcement
- Runs every 6 hours via cron
- Separate handling for **Bug** vs **Feature**:
  - Bug: reminds maintainers to reproduce → confirm → prioritize
  - Feature: reminds to align with roadmap → accept/reject
- Adds `response-needed` label for overdue issues
- Auto-removes label once team responds
- Only comments once (deduplication check)

### 3. `issue-lifecycle.yml` — Full lifecycle automation
- **On `confirmed` label**: removes `needs-triage`, adds `help-wanted`, posts contribution guide for good-first-issues
- **On `accepted` label**: removes `needs-triage`, adds `help-wanted`, invites contributors
- **On claim comment** ("I'd like to work on this" / "我认领"): auto-assigns user, posts quick-start tips tailored to difficulty level
- **On issue close**: thanks external contributors with link to more issues

### 4. `contribution-pool-stats.yml` — Weekly health check
- Runs every Monday 9:00 UTC
- Counts unassigned good-first-issue / intermediate / advanced issues
- If good-first-issues < 10 → creates/updates a tracking issue to alert the team

## Affected areas

- [ ] Desktop app (Electron shell)
- [ ] Controller (backend / API)
- [ ] Web dashboard (React UI)
- [ ] OpenClaw runtime
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] Shared schemas / packages
- [x] Build / CI / Tooling

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes (no TS changes)
- [x] `pnpm lint` passes (no code changes)
- [x] `pnpm test` passes (no logic changes)
- [ ] `pnpm generate-types` run (if API routes/schemas changed) — N/A
- [x] No credentials or tokens in code or logs
- [x] No `any` types introduced (use `unknown` with narrowing)

## Notes for reviewers

- `TEAM_MEMBERS` array in `issue-response-tracker.yml` and `issue-lifecycle.yml` should be reviewed and updated with the current team roster
- The good-first-issue auto-detection is intentionally conservative — it only triggers for bugs that match UX signal patterns and don't involve deep architecture
- All workflows use `actions/github-script@v7` for maintainability (no external marketplace actions)
- The 24h tracker only auto-comments once per issue to avoid spam

author: samvaidya
body: ## Description When block markup is copied from one WordPress site to another, image blocks carry attachment IDs from the source site. The editor assumes these IDs reference local attachments and suppresses the "Upload to Media Library" button. This change piggybacks on the existing `getEntityRecord` call (which already fires when an image block is selected) and adds a `hasFinishedResolution` check. Once resolution confirms the attachment doesn't exist locally, the invalid `id` is cleared from block attributes, allowing the existing external image upload flow to activate correctly. ### How it works 1. Block arrives with `id: 107491` from Site A 2. Existing `useSelect` fires `getEntityRecord('postType', 'attachment', 107491)` - returns 404 3. New `hasFinishedResolution` check confirms resolution is complete (not still loading) 4. New `useEffect` detects: id exists, resolution finished, but no record found - clears the `id` 5. `isExternalImage(undefined, url)` now returns `true` 6. Existing external image upload flow activates - "Upload to Media Library" button appears ### What this doesn't change - Zero new API calls. The REST call was already happening. - `hasFinishedResolution` is a local state check (zero network cost) - Only runs when `isSingleSelected` is true (user clicked on the specific image block) - Valid local images are unaffected ## Future scope - **ID collision detection:** If Site B has a different attachment with the same ID as Site A, the current fix won't detect the mismatch. This was discussed in #74156 and agreed to be out of scope for the MVP. URL matching could address this in a follow-up. - **Other attachment blocks:** As noted by @ramonjd in the issue discussion, this pattern should eventually extend to video, audio, and file blocks. Those blocks don't currently have external upload logic, so extending to them would require building that flow from scratch. ## Testing Instructions 1. Start a local WordPress dev environment 2. Create a new post, switch to Code Editor, paste: ```html ``` 3. Exit code editor, click the image block 4. **Expected:** "Upload to Media Library" button appears in the toolbar 5. Click the button - image uploads successfully 6. **Verify no regression:** Upload a real image via the image block, click it - no upload button appears (correct) 7. **Multiple images:** Paste multiple image blocks with different fake IDs, click each - upload button appears on each Fixes #74156

body:
This pull request introduces a Unit of Work (UoW) pattern to coordinate multi-step database operations in a single transaction, improving data consistency for operations like auto-stop + start and overlap resolution. It adds new interfaces and implementations for `IUnitOfWork` and `IUnitOfWorkFactory`, updates the `WorkEntryService` to use the UoW for all multi-step write operations, and refactors the repository to support both standalone and transactional modes. Documentation is also updated to reflect these architectural changes.

**Unit of Work Pattern Implementation**
- Added `IUnitOfWork` and `IUnitOfWorkFactory` interfaces in `WorkTracker.Application.Interfaces` for transactional coordination of repository operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a505751460af4d2ae9ac3da2200056776fce2b7a18fbadaf44d319883db90ca4R1-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e9160050f96f41330e23c0a2d565f8f7c2a1d8323611f8eab0f5110e9ad25bc6R1-R9)
- Implemented `UnitOfWork` and `UnitOfWorkFactory` in `WorkTracker.Infrastructure.Data`, providing a transactional scope that ensures atomic commits or rollbacks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b0b59d3fe30238d1d8fc610a4705d1e14a98cc6ae66c98f85a59629f0c9918afR1-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6afb16b0d0d8c39e17a829d4292c99cbfd3b9083ddfb9e7a26ec000020819ff1R1-R16)
- Registered `IUnitOfWorkFactory` in DI container for use throughout the application.

**Service and Repository Refactoring**
- Updated `WorkEntryService` to use `IUnitOfWorkFactory` for all multi-step write operations (auto-stop + start, overlap resolution), ensuring atomicity and rollback on failure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c3d91994c347ed3bc984ecc4f922eb849c01024677b660ebafdf1dfa5498b3b4R17-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c3d91994c347ed3bc984ecc4f922eb849c01024677b660ebafdf1dfa5498b3b4L41-R117) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c3d91994c347ed3bc984ecc4f922eb849c01024677b660ebafdf1dfa5498b3b4L226-R281) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c3d91994c347ed3bc984ecc4f922eb849c01024677b660ebafdf1dfa5498b3b4L247-R298) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-c3d91994c347ed3bc984ecc4f922eb849c01024677b660ebafdf1dfa5498b3b4L268-R333)
- Refactored `WorkEntryRepository` to support both factory mode (standalone, each op auto-saves) and shared-context mode (inside UoW, SaveChanges deferred), with internal logic to select the appropriate DbContext.

**Documentation Updates**
- Updated `docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md` and `CLAUDE.md` to document the new Unit of Work pattern, its usage, and how it integrates with the repository and service layers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c8cc1c768f65228fb71f3c6b7aeb9fa144b4b65e8cf514a7e1f10e4bd1077092R146) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7R80)

These changes significantly improve data integrity and transactional consistency for complex operations in the application.

author: domoel
body:
### Description
This PR addresses several stability issues related to room management and power level synchronization within spaces.

### Changes:

**1. Room Alias Resolution (Fixing the "Sigil Bug")**
Previously, commands like `room_setpower ` failed when a room alias (starting with #) was provided instead of a room ID (!).
- **Fix:** Implemented explicit alias resolution using `resolve_room_alias` before executing state changes. This ensures the bot correctly identifies the target room even when users use human-readable aliases.

**2. Robust Room Membership Filtering**
The bot previously attempted to iterate over all child rooms of a space, leading to `403 Forbidden` errors if the bot was not a member of specific rooms.
- **Fix:** Updated `get_space_roomlist ` to intersect the space's child rooms with the bot's `joined_rooms`. The bot now gracefully skips rooms it hasn't joined, preventing failed execution chains. Added an internal log info to track ignored rooms.

**3. Asynchronous Delay and Logic Correction in kick_users**
Found and fixed a bug in the purge loop where a string literal was passed to the sleep function.
- **Fix:** Replaced `time.sleep("sleep")` with `await asyncio.sleep(self.config["sleep"])`. Switching to `asyncio` prevents the entire plugin instance from blocking/freezing during large-scale purge operations.

**4. Add room_id placeholder to join notifications**
- Enhanced the join notification logic to support the {room_id} placeholder.
- This allows administrators to include direct matrix.to deep links in notification messages.
- Added a safety fallback that uses the room ID as the name if the room has no display name set.

**5. Implement crowd moderation and majority-based auto-redaction**

Key Features:
- Reaction-Based Reporting: Users can flag messages by reacting with specific emojis (configurable via `report_emojis`).
- Moderator Notifications: The bot sends an alert with a direct link to the reported message to a designated `notification_room`.
- Automatic Redaction: Introduced `auto_redact_majority` setting. When enabled, the bot counts unique reports. If more than 50% of human members in a room report a message, it is automatically redacted.
- Reliability Safeguards: Implemented set-based tracking to prevent duplicate notifications and processing caused by Matrix sync retries or multiple reactions from the same user.

Configuration:
- `report_emojis`: List of emojis that trigger a report (default: 🚩, ⚠️).
- `auto_redact_majority`: Boolean to enable/disable automated deletion based on community vote.

**6. Enhancement: make room names clickable links in notifications**
improve the UX for moderators and administrators by converting raw room names into clickable HTML links within the bot's notification messages. This allows admins to jump straight into the relevant room with a single click from the notification channel.

- Crowd Moderation (`handle_reactions`): Room names in both the "Message Reported" and "Message Auto-Redacted" alerts are now formatted as clickable HTML anchor tags.
- Join Notifications (`newjoin`): Introduced a new `{room_link}` formatting variable for the `join_notification_message` configuration.
- Backwards Compatibility: Ensured that the existing `{room}` placeholder remains fully functional and continues to output the raw text name. This guarantees that current user configurations (`base-config.yaml`) will not break after updating, while giving them the option to use `{room_link}` moving forward.

### Testing performed:
- **Scenario A:** Verified that setpower now successfully resolves #alias:server to the correct room ID.
- **Scenario B:** Confirmed that the bot no longer throws errors when encountering child rooms it is not a member of.
- **Scenario C:** Verified that the bot remains responsive to other commands while a purge delay is active.
- **Scenario D:** Tested emoji based notification to the notification room and majority based auto redact of message successfully.

author: ratpoisen-cloud
body:
### Motivation
- After a board rebuild (theme or piece-set change) the `#myBoard` DOM was recreated and its reaction handlers were lost because `setupBoardReactionUI` used a persistent guard flag that prevented re-binding. 
- The existing mobile click unbind used a broad `off('click')`, which could remove unrelated handlers and made safe re-initialization unreliable.

### Description
- Add event namespace constants `window.BOARD_REACTION_EVENTS_NS` and `window.BOARD_MOBILE_TAP_EVENTS_NS` for safe add/remove of board-specific handlers. 
- In `setupBoardReactionUI` remove the board-specific guard and always rebind board handlers by first calling `$('#myBoard').off(window.BOARD_REACTION_EVENTS_NS)` and then attaching namespaced `contextmenu`, `touchstart`, `touchend`, `touchcancel`, and `touchmove` handlers so they reattach to the newly created `#myBoard` DOM. 
- In `attachMobileClickHandler` replace the coarse `off('click')` with a namespaced `off('click' + window.BOARD_MOBILE_TAP_EVENTS_NS)` and attach namespaced click handlers to avoid removing other click handlers and to prevent duplicate bindings. 
- Preserve global handlers on `document` and `window` (they remain guarded so they are not rebound repeatedly). 

### Testing
- Syntax check: ran `node --check js/board-ui.js` and it completed successfully.

author: copilot
body:
Ports route handlers from 6 Cloudflare Workers into AWS Lambda entry points under the new `lambdas/` directory, using the shared `bootstrap()` service container (`packages/shared/src/platform/aws/`) in place of CF env bindings.

## Structure (per lambda)
- `src/handler.ts` — error boundary, dispatches to `route(event)` or `processXxx(event)`
- `src/routes.ts` — module-level `bootstrap()` singleton, `extractAuth()`, pattern-matches on `rawPath + method`, returns `APIGatewayProxyResultV2`
- `src/processor.ts` — SQS / EventBridge-specific processing where the lambda has a non-HTTP trigger

## Lambdas created

| Lambda | Source Worker | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `core-api` | `core-api/src/` | HTTP — tenants, events, flags, auth |
| `compliance-api` | `compliance-worker/src/` | HTTP — evidence CRUD, policy gen/eval, CDT scoring, snapshots |
| `orchestrator` | `ai-orchestrator/src/` | HTTP + SQS — events, agents, workflows, JML, dead-letter; step-task queue consumer |
| `onboarding-api` | `onboarding/src/` | HTTP — start/submit/status, question generation |
| `scheduler` | `scheduler-worker/index.js` | HTTP + EventBridge — manual trigger + cron job fan-out |
| `slack-handler` | `slack-approval-worker/index.js` | HTTP — Slack approval with HMAC-SHA256 verification |
| `dlq-processor` | `ai-orchestrator/src/routes/dead-letter.ts` | SQS — DLQ consumer; persists failures, updates workflow status, writes audit trail |

## CF → AWS binding translations

```
env.DB.prepare(...)         → pg.Pool (DATABASE_URL)
env.KV_SESSIONS.get(...)    → svc.sessionRepo.get(...)     // DynamoDB
env.KV_CACHE.get/set(...)   → svc.cacheRepo.get/set(...)   // DynamoDB
env.EVIDENCE_BUCKET.put(…)  → svc.evidenceRepo.put(...)    // S3
env.STEP_TASKS.send(...)    → svc.queueRepo.send(...)       // SQS
requireTenant(request, env) → extractAuth(event, svc.authRepo)
```

body:
## Description

`createSpellModifier` was called with `modifier: 0` in three formulas — `threatOnBuff`, `threatOnBuffOrDamage`, and `threatOnCastRollbackOnMiss`. This set `spellModifier.value = 0` in the UI tooltip metadata, incorrectly showing a **0× multiplier** instead of the implicit **1×**.

Fixed by using `modifier: 1` in all three, which causes `createSpellModifier` to omit the `value` field (it only sets it when the multiplier meaningfully differs from 1). The UI then defaults to `value ?? 1`.

Config versions bumped: era → 16, sod → 13, tbc → 14.

author: ajaybervanshi
body:
💡 **What:** Added `.limit(1)` to Supabase `.select("id", count="exact")` database calls inside `src/core/learning_engine.py` (`get_success_rate` method).

🎯 **Why:** By default, calling `.select("id", count="exact")` without a pagination limit causes PostgREST/Supabase to download all matched rows over the network before returning the count metadata. This represents an O(N) network and memory bottleneck that scales poorly as tables grow large.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces network payload overhead from O(N) rows to exactly 1 row during count queries, significantly speeding up database interaction latencies and lowering process memory consumption.

🔬 **Measurement:** The exact row count continues to be properly populated into the `.count` attribute of the response object, as verified by unit tests mocking the chained API wrapper (`test_limit2.py` in trace). The `limit(1)` is exclusively applied to the rows returned, keeping the response metadata fully intact.

author: avelino
body:
fixed: #51

The proxy used to serialize everything through a single ProxyServer mutex held across backend I/O, so one slow backend or dead client could freeze every other session. Under opencode it also leaked child processes (13 chroma-mcp, 4 roam-tui, etc) because shutdown timeouts would silently give up and Command wasn't reaped on drop.

Rewrote the hot path around Arc<McpClient> and a three-phase dispatch that never holds the proxy lock across await: resolve routing under a brief lock, connect (if needed) with the lock released, then call_tool fully outside the lock. Transport trait is now &self + Sync so a single client instance is shared across concurrent tasks; StdioTransport runs a writer task + a reader task with a pending-id map, so multiple in-flight requests on the same backend multiplex through one pipe. Discovery moved out of the proxy lock entirely with its own discovery_lock to dedupe concurrent batches without blocking request handlers for already-discovered backends. Reaper runs in parallel via JoinSet, respects a warm-up grace so fresh backends aren't killed before first use, and force-kills via kill_on_drop when shutdown stalls. Every tokio Command has kill_on_drop(true) so orphans are impossible by construction. SSE legacy path bounds tx.send with a 5s timeout and evicts wedged sessions instead of pinning handlers forever; ping task uses try_send. HTTP listener binds with TCP keepalive 30s/10s so dead clients are detected in ~60s instead of 2h, and a per-request proxy timeout (MCP_PROXY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, default 120s) is the final bound.

- Expose and decouple parts of the trading engine to allow dependency injection and easier unit testing.
- Add additional API endpoints and include extra public assets in the Docker image for new UI pages.

### Description
- Introduced `app-server.js` which encapsulates HTTP server creation with normalized path handling, SSE client management, robust error handling, and multiple API routes including `/opportunities`, `/dividends`, `/risk`, `/daily-brief`, `/company/:ticker`, and `/analysis/:ticker` as well as legacy `api/*` variants.
- Updated `server.js` to use `createServer({ engine, publicDir })`, parse `PORT` with `Number()`, and simplify lifecycle/shutdown logic by delegating request handling to `app-server.js`.
- Made `calculateRSI` and `buildFallbackDecision` exported in `trading-engine.js` and added dependency injection for `fetch`, `writeFile`, and `yahoo` client via constructor `dependencies`, and switched `persistResults` to use `this.writeFileFn`.
- Updated `Dockerfile` to copy `app-server.js` and several new directories (`analysis`, `data`, `dividends`, `explainer`, `fundamentals`, `portfolio`, `risk`, `scanner`) into the image.

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or executed as part of this change.

author: itsakeyfut
body:
## Summary

Adds `FilterGraphBuilder::spill_suppress()` to reduce green/blue color spill on the edges of keyed subjects. The method wraps FFmpeg's `hue` filter with a fixed hue shift (`h=0`) and saturation set to `1.0 - strength`, globally desaturating the spill hue region. A `strength` of `0.0` leaves the image unchanged; `1.0` fully desaturates the frame.

## Changes

- `filter_step.rs`: Added `SpillSuppress { key_color: String, strength: f32 }` variant with `filter_name() → "hue"` and `args() → "h=0:s=(1.0-strength)"`
- `compositing.rs`: Added `spill_suppress(key_color, strength) -> Self` builder method
- `builder/mod.rs`: Added `strength` validation in `[0.0, 1.0]` with two unit tests (`spill_suppress_out_of_range_strength_should_return_invalid_config`, `spill_suppress_negative_strength_should_return_invalid_config`)
- `push_pull_tests.rs`: Added integration test `spill_suppress_should_reduce_green_cast_on_subject_edges` verifying the U chroma plane moves toward neutral after full-strength desaturation

## Related Issues

Closes #340

- **Test coverage**: 145 → 149 tests; global lines 87% → **99.46%**, global funcs → **100%**
- **ESLint**: migrated to unified `typescript-eslint` v8.58.1 with `strictTypeChecked` preset
- **CI security**: added `bun audit`, `trivy` container scan (pinned to `@v0.35.0`), `gitleaks` history scan (pinned to `@v2.3.9`)
- **Pre-commit**: added `gitleaks protect --staged` before lint-staged
- **Router refactor**: extracted `cleanupStaleIdempotencyEntries` as pure function; router.ts funcs 83% → 100%
- **Latent bug fix**: `retryWithBackoff({ maxAttempts: 0 })` no longer throws literal `undefined`
- **Project setup**: `.nvmrc` (Node 22), Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` on `/healthz`, `init-options.json` → timestamp branch numbering

### Testing & coverage
- New `test/core/prompt-builder.test.ts`, `test/utils/assertions.ts` (new `expectToReject` helper)
- Extended `fetcher.test.ts` (9% → 100%), `formatter.test.ts` (67% → 100%), `router.test.ts` (concurrency limit tests with try/finally)

## Notes for reviewer

### Intentional mechanical fixes in src/*.ts
The ESLint `strictTypeChecked` preset surfaced several mechanical issues in existing code that were fixed as part of the migration (not behavioral changes):

- `src/app.ts`: arrow bodies expanded for `no-confusing-void-expression`

Only reflects the intentional dependency swap:
- Removed: `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin@^8.56.0`, `@typescript-eslint/parser@^8.56.0`
- Added: `typescript-eslint@^8.56.0` (unified package with both as dependencies)

1. **#7 — DI refactor for `checkout.ts` and `executor.ts`**. FR-007 and FR-008 explicitly required module-level unit tests at ≥90% per-file coverage. Both were formally **deferred** because Bun's `$` built-in cannot be intercepted by `mock.module` and because `mock.module` for `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` persists globally across test files (it would break `router.test.ts`). After the initial push, GitHub Copilot and CodeRabbit posted 8 review comments; all 8 were validated against the code as real issues and fixed in Phase 8. body:
## Problem

The `.catch` handler in `index.js` only logs `err.message`, which is empty for certain Sequelize/MySQL connection errors (e.g. network timeouts, ECONNREFUSED, access denied). This makes it impossible to diagnose why the service crashes on startup in Railway.

## Solution

Expanded the catch block to separately log `err.message`, `err.code`, the full error object, the stack trace, and the resolved connection details (host, port, user, database name from env vars). This surfaces the actual failure reason — whether it's a DNS/network issue, wrong credentials, or a missing database — without any ambiguity.

### Changes
- **Modified** `index.js`

body:
The ingest pipeline was brittle with real-world phone video inputs (MOV, HEVC, temp filenames, missing extensions) and normalization could exhaust worker memory on large files due to expensive encode settings and unbounded ffmpeg output buffering.

## `libs/video/ffmpeg.py`

- **`NormalizationError`** replaces bare `CalledProcessError` — carries `returncode` and `stderr` (trimmed to last 2 KB) so job error fields stay readable without ballooning storage.
- **`probe_media_streams()`** — new function; inspects actual media content via ffprobe independent of filename/extension. Returns `StreamInfo` (`has_video`, `has_audio`, `video_codec`, `audio_codec`, `container_format`).
- **Lower-cost `normalize_video()` defaults:**
  - `superfast` preset instead of `fast`; CRF 28 instead of 23
  - Resolution capped at 1280×720 (aspect-ratio-preserving scale filter, only downscales)
  - FPS capped at 30; thread count capped at 2
  - `-map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0?` — optional audio map handles silent clips without erroring out
  - `-loglevel error` prevents buffering megabytes of per-frame progress lines in `capture_output`

```python
# Before: CalledProcessError with no useful context
# After:
except NormalizationError as exc:
    # exc.returncode, exc.stderr available; message already carries trimmed stderr
    logger.debug("ffmpeg full stderr for video %d:\n%s", video_id, exc.stderr)
    raise
```

## `apps/worker/jobs/process_video.py`

- Calls `probe_media_streams()` on the local source file **before** normalization — logs codec/container, raises a clear `ValueError` with container info if no video stream is present (catches corrupt uploads, audio-only files, etc.).
- Specific `NormalizationError` handler logs full stderr at DEBUG before re-raising, so the trimmed message lands in `job.error` / `run.error` while full context is in logs.

## Tests (`tests/test_video_ingest_robustness.py`)

33 new focused tests covering:
- `NormalizationError` attributes and message trimming
- `normalize_video` command construction (preset, CRF, threads, FPS cap, scale filter, loglevel, optional audio map)
- Extension-agnostic inputs: `.MOV`, `.tmp`, no extension
- `probe_media_streams` stream detection, codec/container extraction, failure path, extension independence, iPhone HEVC detection
- Worker raises clear error on no-video-stream source; surfaces `NormalizationError` in `job.error`; accepts iPhone MOV and temp filenames end-to-end

In the discussion for that issue, I made out that this would be a bit tricky :

> But there's a problem : a label exists on the shader even if it hasn't been overridden by the ShaderAssignment node, so we currently can't know if you used that feature or not.

author: olvikt
body:
### Motivation
- `MyOrders::render()` previously mixed hot runtime reads (active orders, runtime/map) with cold aggregate reads (completed stats/earnings and nearby aggregates), causing expensive work on every poll and observable spikes in `my_orders_render.elapsed_ms`.
- The goal is to make the active/orders poll path cheap and fast while keeping stats/earnings as a separate, bounded-stale cold path without changing canonical runtime semantics or UX.

### Description
- Split `MyOrders` render into a hot runtime pane and a cold stats pane so completed stats/earnings are only loaded when `activeTab === 'stats'`, preserving all runtime actions and contracts in the hot path (`app/Livewire/Courier/MyOrders.php`).
- Added explicit observability markers and dimensions: `my_orders_runtime_render`, `my_orders_stats_render`, and extended `my_orders_render` with `runtime_elapsed_ms`, `stats_elapsed_ms`, `active_tab`, and counts to make hot vs cold costs visible.
- Isolated cold-path failures by catching errors from `CourierCompletedOrdersDailyStatsQuery`, setting `statsPaneUnavailable=true`, logging `my_orders_stats_render_failed`, and showing a non-blocking degraded notice in the stats UI (`resources/views/livewire/courier/my-orders.blade.php`).
- Reduced repeated nearby-area aggregation on the hot path by caching the nearby summary with a bounded TTL (`courier:{id}:my-orders:nearby-area-summary`) and added `COURIER_MY_ORDERS_NEARBY_SUMMARY_TTL_SECONDS` config (`config/courier_runtime.php`).
- Added read-semantics regression tests and documentation: `tests/Feature/Courier/CourierMyOrdersHotColdReadPathTest.php` and `docs/my-orders-hot-cold-read-path-evidence.md`, which assert that the orders tab does not hit `courier_earnings`, the stats tab does, and that stats failures do not break the hot pane.

### Testing
- Added tests: `tests/Feature/Courier/CourierMyOrdersHotColdReadPathTest.php` which includes assertions for hot-path query absence, stats-path query presence after tab switch, and isolated failure handling; these tests are included in the PR.
- Ran quick automated checks: `php -l app/Livewire/Courier/MyOrders.php`, `php -l tests/Feature/Courier/CourierMyOrdersHotColdReadPathTest.php`, and `php -l config/courier_runtime.php`, all of which reported no syntax errors.
- Attempted to run `php artisan test ...` for the feature suite but the test run failed in this environment due to missing `vendor/autoload.php` (CI / local environment should run the full test suite where vendor deps are present).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Fixes several bugs found via code review of recent commits: **Critical: Deauth frames sent on wrong WiFi channel.** After `WiFi.scanNetworks()` the radio ends up on an unpredictable channel. `sendDeauth()` never switched to the target AP's channel, so deauth frames were almost always transmitted on the wrong channel — making the attack non-functional. This PR stores `WiFi.channel(i)` during target selection and calls `esp_wifi_set_channel()` before transmitting. **Deauth frame missing reason code.** The `deauthFrame[26]` array only had 24 bytes initialized; bytes 24-25 (reason code) defaulted to `0x0000` which is "Reserved" per IEEE 802.11. Now explicitly set to `0x0007` (Class 3 frame from nonassociated STA). The initializer is also reformatted with per-field comments for readability. **Missing X coordinate flip in `wifiScan()` touch handler.** Only `ty` was flipped but not `tx`, inconsistent with `main.cpp` which flips both axes. Added `tx` flip and X bounds checking. **Dead BLE declarations removed.** `blePredator(int mode)` and `stopBleSpam()` were declared in `ble_utils.h` but never defined in `ble_utils.cpp`. These would cause linker errors if called. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify deauth frame byte layout is still correct** — the initializer was restructured for readability. Confirm the 26-byte total and that field offsets (source at 10, BSSID at 16, seq at 22, reason at 24) are preserved. Note: source/BSSID initializers changed from `0xFF`/mixed to `0x00` but are overwritten by the loop — verify that's harmless. - [ ] **Test on hardware that `esp_wifi_set_channel(target_channel, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE)` works correctly before `esp_wifi_80211_tx()`** — there's no error checking on the return value. If this call requires promiscuous mode or a specific WiFi state, deauth may still fail silently. - [ ] **Confirm `WiFi.channel(i)` returns a valid channel after `scanNetworks()` completes** — scan results should persist, but verify on the actual ESP32-S3 board. - [ ] **Flash and test end-to-end**: scan for networks, select a target, trigger deauth, and verify frames are actually transmitted on the correct channel (e.g. with a WiFi monitor on the target AP's channel). ### Notes - These changes could not be compiled or tested without the PlatformIO toolchain and the GUITION ESP32-4848S040 hardware. All fixes are based on code review only. - `WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE` is used for the secondary channel parameter — this should be fine for deauth but may need adjustment if targeting APs using HT40 channel bonding. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cea435d3c47e48c6aeab8319924b2dc5 Requested by: @AlienKnalKoe ---

author: lml2468
body:
## Summary

Fixes #63643

> **AI-assisted PR** — built with Claude (Anthropic). Degree of testing: fully tested (11 tests pass across 3 new test files). The fix was authored by an AI agent team and cross-reviewed before submission.

Long-running gateway instances (24/7 deployments) exhibit steady memory growth of ~15-20 MB/hour even when idle. This PR plugs three independent memory leaks found via deep code audit.

## Root Cause

Three module-level `Map` instances grow monotonically without cleanup:

### 1. `seqByRun` in `agent-events.ts`

`clearAgentRunContext(runId)` deletes the run context from `runContextById` but **forgets to delete** the corresponding sequence counter from `seqByRun`. Every completed agent run (including heartbeats) leaves a permanent `runId → number` entry.

**Fix:** Delete `seqByRun[runId]` in `clearAgentRunContext`.

### 2. `controlPlaneBuckets` in `control-plane-rate-limit.ts`

Each unique `deviceId|clientIp` combination creates a rate-limit bucket. Buckets are reset when their window expires, but the **map entry is never removed**. With connection churn (especially `connId` fallback keys), the map grows without bound.

**Fix:** Add `pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets()` that removes buckets whose window expired more than 5 minutes ago. Called from the existing 60s gateway maintenance timer.

### 3. `TRANSCRIPT_SESSION_KEY_CACHE` in `session-transcript-key.ts`

Each unique transcript file path is cached permanently with no TTL or size limit.

**Fix:** Add a 256-entry FIFO cap using Map insertion order. (Note: this is insertion-order eviction, not recency-based LRU — for this use case where entries are resolved once and rarely re-queried, FIFO is sufficient and simpler.)

## Testing
- **agent-events regression test:** Verifies that `clearAgentRunContext` resets the sequence counter (seq restarts from 1), proving the old entry was deleted.
- **control-plane-rate-limit test:** Verifies stale bucket pruning and empty-map safety.
All 11 tests pass.

## AI-assisted Checklist

- [x] Marked as AI-assisted in the PR description
- [x] Degree of testing noted: 11 tests pass across 3 test areas
- [x] Fix reviewed and understood by the submitting agent before submission
- [x] Bot review conversations addressed (aisle-research-bot: replied with rationale; greptile + Codex inline comments: replied with FIFO vs LRU explanation)

author: gereon77
body: After a server restart the DatabaseCache survives, leaving connected-user entries with no corresponding live WebSocket. Instead of a whole-dict TTL or an admin endpoint, add a _last_active_at (UTC ISO) field to each entry that is refreshed on every connect. A _prune_stale() helper evicts any entry missing the timestamp (covers pre-existing cache entries) or older than 12 hours. Pruning runs on every read and write so cleanup is lazy but guaranteed. Also clamp _count to never go below 0 and use an INTERNAL_KEYS constant to strip both _count and _last_active_at before broadcasting the user list to clients.

author: tszulist-hbn
body:
Addresses https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/issues/3081

Sparse Triton ops (`scatter_mm`, `bsr_dense_addmm`, `bsr_dense_mm`, `sampled_addmm`, `bsr_softmax`, `scaled_dot_product_attention`) are hardcoded to CUDA via `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` calls and a CUDA-only `check_device` guard. This prevents them from running on Intel XPU devices that have a working Triton backend (`triton.backends.intel`).

This PR introduces a `_get_device_name()` helper in `_triton_ops_meta.py` that returns the current accelerator's device name for use as a Triton tuning cache key, preferring XPU when available and falling back to CUDA. It replaces all 7 hardcoded `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` calls across both files and updates `check_device` to accept `"xpu"` in addition to `"cuda"`.

**Tested on:** Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550 (PVC). With this change, `TestSparseCompressedTritonKernelsXPU` goes from 38 passed / 44 failed to 58 passed / 24 failed / 93 skipped. The remaining 24 failures are due to Intel Triton compiler limitations (blocksize 16/16x32, bfloat16/float16/int8 crash with `PassManager::run failed`) and a missing native `sparse_sampled_addmm` kernel for `SparseCsrXPU`, both of which are pre-existing issues unrelated to this change.

This PR was authored with the help of AI (GitHub Copilot / Claude).
