author: lucasmusikgladjen
body:
## Summary

Three linked UX fixes to the Product Area editor.

### 1. Collapsible sektion / product / solution cards

Adds a small `CollapsibleCard` primitive used by `ContentBlocksEditor`, `ProductsEditor` and `SolutionsEditor`. The header row (index + inline title input + `▲▼` + `✕`) stays visible and interactive when collapsed so renaming, reordering and removing items still works without expanding the body. A chevron toggles the body.

**Default-open rule:** filled items start collapsed (compact list view when opening an existing PA), new/empty items start open so the user can start typing immediately after clicking `+ Lägg till`.

### 2. Hero right column as an either/or

The Hero editor used to render the NPI card fields, benefits textarea and image URL input as a single long list even though the rendered page only shows one of them (the PHP plugin's priority: `npi > benefits > image`). Now mirrors LP's `SidebarEditor` pattern: a **"Höger kolumn"** `FieldSelect` with `Ingen / NPI-kort / Benefits / Bild`, and only the selected variant's fields render.

- Initial selection is derived from state on mount using the PHP plugin's priority rule, so loading an existing PA picks the variant the record actually uses.
- Switching clears the now-hidden fields (`npiTitle`/`npiDescription`/`npiImage`/`npiLink` when leaving NPI, `heroBenefits` when leaving Benefits, `heroImage` when leaving Image) so the preview and the saved record always match the user's explicit choice.

### 3. Quick-nav pills wrap instead of clipping

The 7 PA section labels (Hero, Innehåll, Produkter, Lösningar, Kontakt, Dokumentation, Inställningar) can't all fit horizontally in a 380px editor pane. The old `overflow-x-auto` container let them scroll but the last pill (`Inställningar`) visibly clipped against the right edge — see user screenshot. Switched to `flex-wrap` with `gap-y-1` so pills drop to a second row when there isn't room. No horizontal scroll fiddling, nothing hidden from view.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an existing PA with 5+ products → all products render as collapsed rows, a compact list instead of a wall of forms
- [ ] Click `+ Lägg till produkt` → new product opens expanded ready to type
- [ ] Click the chevron on an existing collapsed product → body opens; `▲▼` and `✕` still work on both collapsed and expanded states
- [ ] Same flow for Innehåll sektioner and Lösningar cards
- [ ] Open a PA with an existing NPI card → Hero editor shows `Höger kolumn: NPI-kort` and the NPI fields
- [ ] Switch to `Benefits` → NPI fields disappear and `heroBenefits` textarea shows; preview updates to benefits box
- [ ] Switch back to `NPI-kort` → must retype (the previous NPI fields were cleared on the switch, which is the intended behaviour)
- [ ] Open editor on a narrow monitor → Inställningar pill is fully visible (no clipping), likely on a second row

author: scobru
body:
💡 **What:** The optimization implemented is introducing a `seenMessageIdsRef` Set to keep track of known message IDs and replacing the `Array.some` forward loop with an `O(1)` ID check, accompanied by a bounded reverse loop for fuzzy checking (time, sender, content). Furthermore, mutations to the `Set` were correctly hoisted outside the React pure updater `setMessages` function to avoid bugs related to Concurrent Rendering / Strict Mode.

🎯 **Why:** The previous code used `.some()` to scan the entire array of messages on each incoming message. For a large array (e.g. 10k items), receiving a chunk of new messages (e.g. 1000) would cause UI freezing because it turned into an $O(N^2)$ algorithm. 

📊 **Measured Improvement:** The `Array.some` implementation took roughly `317ms` to process `1,000` new messages in a chat history of `10,000` items. My newly implemented `Set + Safe Backwards` logic brought it down to `12.42 ms`, achieving a speedup of `~25x` while preventing React component state bugs.

## What changed

- Added a `type` field to every experiment in `data/experiments.json` with three values: `commercial`, `tool`, `personal`
- Updated `agents/market-research.md` to branch on type at a new Step 0, before any analysis begins:
  - **commercial** → full TAM/SAM/SOM analysis (existing behavior, unchanged)
  - **tool** → lightweight Problem & Value Assessment — who has the problem, what do people do instead, what value does it deliver. No market sizing.
  - **personal** → brief Personal Value Note — first-person reflection on the need, what already exists, what success looks like
- Adjusted scoring guidance so Business Opportunity is not inflated against the commercial rubric for tool/personal experiments

## Why

The market-research agent was generating full TAM/SAM/SOM calculations for every experiment regardless of whether it made sense — e.g. a $600M TAM for an internal workflow tool. Experiment type gives the agent the context it needs to produce the right depth of analysis.

## Current classification

All 10 existing experiments have been classified. `web-to-figma-grabber` is the only `tool`; everything else is `commercial`. No `personal` experiments exist yet but the type is ready for future use.

author: copilot
body:
Bootstraps the repo with `pcvr_edtech.py` — a Pythonista 3 iOS app combining a 5-lesson PCVR curriculum with an integrated arcade shooter demo (Warp Protocol). The prior codebase had no source files; this implements the full interactive experience described in the issue.

## Scene architecture
- **State machine**: `SPLASH → ENTER_NAME → PCVR_INTRO → LESSON(0-4) → GAME_INTRO → GAME / GAMEOVER`
- Each state transition runs a `Transition` fade-out → state swap → fade-in; no state flicker
- `slide_t` cubic-ease drives per-scene slide-in; lesson body lines stagger their fade-in with per-line delays

## Visual & interaction effects
- **Screen shake**: `self.shake` exponentially decays each frame; offset propagated to every draw call
- **Button press**: white flash + HSV particle burst (`spawn_burst`) + `sound.play_effect()` — different clip per transition type (`arcade:Powerup_1/2/3`, `digital:PowerUp6/7/8`, etc.)
- **Themed backgrounds**: each lesson has a unique `hue`; PCVR overview slowly oscillates hue over time; game sectors shift HSV brightness
- **Pulsating elements**: glow ring (PCVR overview), button border pulse, title scale oscillation via `math.sin`, warp flash on sector change

## Learning content (5 lessons)
What is PCVR · Core hardware · GPU rendering pipeline · Writing a VR loop · Optimization tips

## Warp Protocol arcade demo
Full port of the Atlas Omega game: gravity mechanics, inverted-gravity mode at 7000 pts, 4 themed sectors (Neon / Void / Golden Bull / Crimson Core), seeker/bomber enemies, shield/bull/health/coin power-ups, frenzy mode, glitch offset. Game-over: short tap = retry, long hold = back to lessons.

```python
# Entry point
if __name__ == '__main__':
    run(PCVREdTech(), PORTRAIT)
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Upgrade the PCVR Educational App by integrating the following features:

### Visual and Interactive Enhancements

1. **Button Press Effects**:
   - Add unique sound effects every time a scene transitions.
   - Trigger dynamic screen shake on button presses.

2. **Enhanced Particle Effects**:
   - Increase particle count on every button interaction.
   - Use vibrant color flashes during transitions for more impact.

3. **Animated Text Effects**:
   - Introduce fade-in or slide-in text animations for every new scene.

4. **Themed Backgrounds by Scene**:
   - Change atmospheric background effects to match the theme of each page/lesson.

5. **Dynamic Sound Effects**:
   - Use varied sound effects based on scene type and user interaction.

6. **Vibrancy Adjustments**:
   - Create pulsating or glowing elements that interact with user inputs.

### Integration Into Learning Framework

- Retain the current flow structure with the start screen, PCVR education overview, learning pages, and gameplay demo.
